reason: The cited evidence (E2, E3, E4) describes precipitation strengthening and dual-phase deformation in Al0.7CoCrFeNi, a different alloy system, and does not provide any data on B2 precipitation in HfZrTiTa0.53, its effect on stacking fault energy, or its impact on tensile ductility and energy release. E1 explicitly states that phase stabilities in this alloy are uncertain and that B2 ordering was observed during quenching, not from a deliberate aging treatment. Thus, the key premises lack specific prior evidence and are largely speculative.
premises: Aging HfZrTiTa0.53 at 550–650 °C will induce nanoscale coherent B2 precipitates.
These B2 precipitates will lower the generalized stacking fault energy.
Lowered stacking fault energy will promote deformation twinning and enhance dislocation mobility.
Enhanced twinning and dislocation mobility will increase uniform tensile elongation from ~13.5% to ≥20%.
The dual-phase structure will preserve yield strength >780 MPa and impact-triggered energy release.
